lines.text: Do you know how a cat lands on its feet? It flips itself over in mid-air, with nothing to push against.
Falling upside down, the cat bends in the middle, so its front half and back half can turn separately.
First it tucks its front legs in, and stretches its back legs out. The front spins round fast. The back barely moves.
Then it swaps. Front legs out, back legs in, and the back half catches up.
Tucking in makes things spin faster, like a figure skater pulling in their arms. The cat uses that trick on each half in turn.
A super flexible spine, and loose collarbones, make the twist possible. Kittens start doing it at around three to four weeks old.
Then it spreads out like a little parachute, and lands on bent legs to soak up the hit.
So a cat doesn't cheat physics. It just turns in two halves.
